    Part 2 · Stage by stage

    What do we fill at each stage, and where does the simulator feed it?

    Part 2 · the plan

    Facts first, causes next, tests before any move

    1. Record and definesymptom, urgency, IS / IS NOT, statement
    2. Explorefundamentals, fishbone, falsifiable hypotheses
    3. Screen and planS / D / N, then the cheapest decisive test
    4. Evidence from the OTSrun, snapshot and log

    Stages 0 and 1

    Write what was seen, with numbers and times, then decide the urgency

    • 0.2–0.3 symptom and the operator's trends.
    • R.4 normal versus failure modes.
    • 1.3–1.4 time-critical? run, safe-park or shut down.

    Interactive · Define, 2.7 and 2.11

    A problem statement you can test has five parts

    The IS / IS NOT table supplies each part; the statement names the symptom, never a cause.

    Stage 3 · 3.2 and 3.4

    Every cause idea goes on one of the six bones

    • Bones come from the pack: suction, pumps, legs, instruments, delivery, people.
    • Each idea becomes a hypothesis in 3.6.
    • Write it as “if … then we should observe …”.

    Interactive · Plan 4.3 · click a cell

    One D on a solid fact kills a hypothesis

    Screen with facts before spending money: what survives is what the plant test must split.

    Interactive · Plan 4.6 and 4.8

    Pick the tests: coverage up, cost and hours down

    A look before a move: the field round costs little and splits five hypotheses; the isolation test settles the rest.

    OTS data & evidence

    Three pulls from the running simulator become datasets

    • Run: every DCS trend, 10 s.
    • Snapshot: each tag against design.
    • Log: alarms and operator moves.
    • Outside the tab: Data export CSV, dropped here.

    Pull again after every plant test and give the run the role “Plant test”.

    Part 2 · summary

    What part 2 settled

    • Record facts with numbers before any idea.
    • State the symptom in five parts, IS / IS NOT behind it.
    • Ideas on bones, then falsifiable hypotheses.
    • Screen S / D / N, then plan the cheapest decisive test.
    • Run, snapshot and log carry the evidence.

    Part 3 · the plan

    The worked example, loaded from Worked examples

    1. The casethe situation the trainee gets
    2. The runwhat the trends show, and what they cannot
    3. The pump curveflow from two local gauges
    4. Tests, fix, reportverdicts, ledger, Word and slides

    TE-1 “The lazy twin” · read first

    The situation the trainee is given

    TE-1 is a worked case for everyone, not a graded exercise: open it from Case & team ▸ Worked examples ▸ Open example, after trying it yourself.

    Interactive · drag the time

    55 minutes of TE-1 on the simulator

    The DCS shows a short flow with the valve wide open; the local gauge on idle B is the reading that splits the hypotheses.

    Interactive · R.3 and 3.2 calculator

    Two local gauges give the flow the pump makes

    Pump curve$\Delta H = H_0 s^2 - kQ^2$

    $Q=\sqrt{(H_0 s^2-\Delta H)/k}$ with $H_0$ = 45.0 m, $s$ = 1, $k$ = 0.0663 m/(L/s)²: pump flow above the meter means liquid leaves between them.

    Stage 5 · Do it

    Each test is run, pulled and compared with its prediction

    • T-1 field round: gauges, both shafts, a phone call.
    • T-2 close V205 for 15 min: flow back to 14.0 L/s.
    • WH-1 survives; six hypotheses killed.

    One cause is left standing; now it must be fixed and kept from coming back.

    Stages 5 and 6

    Fix now, repair for good, stop it coming back

      Outputs

      Save the project, then let the workbook write the report and slides

      • Save a .woods.json; Open continues it anywhere.
      • Word report: every filled sub-step in stage order.
      • Slides: 16:9 team deck from your work.
      • Hand in the .woods.json with the report.

      Part 3 · summary

      What part 3 settled

      • TE-1 opens from Worked examples, never by itself.
      • DCS shows the symptom; field gauges split causes.
      • Two gauges and the curve give the pump flow.
      • Two cheap tests confirmed one hypothesis of seven.
      • Save, report and slides close the case.

      This deck

      Key Takeaways

      1

      Record the symptom with numbers before naming a cause.

      2

      Write each hypothesis so a fact can kill it.

      3

      Look before you move; plan every test before touching the plant.

      4

      Pull the run after every test and compare it with the prediction.

      5

      Save the .woods.json; the workbook writes the report and slides.
